Subject: Passing Input Variables Through Code


Perhaps this is a question for the manipulatr group, but here goes...

Problem: I want to have an Shiny input, which is then passed to some dplyr code to:

    1) group/summarize a data set and,
    2) plot the data with ggplot2

I'll sketch the problem w/ minimal code for simplicity:

Given:

UI.R
input$my_variable
plotOutput(my_plot)
server.R
df  ##the data set; dim is O(1,000 rows x 40 vars)

cut <- group_by_(df, ~my_variable) ##this is do-able thanks to dplyr 0.3

summary <- summarise(cut, ...) ##no problem here

my_plot <- renderplot(ggplot(summary, aes(x =~my_variable,...) ##ggplot doesn't like this

Qs
Is there a workaround?
Can ggvis do this?
Should I generally be transitioning away from ggplot2 to ggvis anyway?

parts:
Here you go; pasted below and attached.
The code fails of course, but I tried to implement your recommendation.  I think I'm missing something fundamental about NSE/SE:

ui.R
shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
selectInput("choice",
                 "Choices",
                 c('am','gear','carb')),
plotOutput("plot1")
)
)

server.R
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


shinyServer(function(input, output) {
observe({
cut <- group_by_(mtcars,input$choice)
summary <- summarise(cut, n = n())
output$plot1 <- ggplot(summary, aes(x = input$choice, y = n)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity")
})
  }
)

parts:
One more try...your server file can be:

# Solution based on Sebastian Kranz's response to SO question: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/21208801/group-by-multiple-columns-in-dplyr-using-string-vector-input
# https://gist.github.com/skranz/9681509

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
#' Internal function used by s_filter, s_select etc.
eval.string.dplyr = function(.data, .fun.name, ...) {
  args = list(...)
  args = unlist(args)
  code = paste0(.fun.name,"(.data,", paste0(args, collapse=","), ")")
  df = eval(parse(text=code,srcfile=NULL))
  df  
}
s_group_by = function(.data, ...) {
  eval.string.dplyr(.data,"group_by", ...)
}

shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {
  sub=reactive(mtcars%>%s_group_by(input$choice)%>%summarise(n=n()))
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot(ggplot(sub(),aes_string(x = input$choice, y = "n")) + geom_bar(stat = "identity"))
  
  })
